changes: Added flagged-provisional ID 3552 for Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance. The source reports: The paper reports a fully dynamic single-edge insertion/deletion maximum-cardinality-search ordering algorithm using probe then repair, with validity and equality to canonical recomputation, locality and executable refinement, and unit-cost n insertion/n+1 deletion bounds; it also gives a sufficient common-ordering condition and matching/flip corollaries. Primary source: https://data.palomar-registry.org/entries/PALOMAR-2026-10-04-000009-v1.json. Further checking: Further checking: Obtain independent algorithms/graph-theory review; audit novelty and the exact model against static and dynamic MCS literature; check locality, cost, stability, theorem/manuscript correspondence, unit-cost limitations, exact human/model allocation, and independently replay the formal package.

Added flagged-provisional ID 3553 for Long-time Korteweg-de Vries approximation for the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou system. The source reports: The paper reports that, as the lattice spacing h tends to zero, general solutions of the infinite Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou system are approximated in L2 by two counter-propagating Korteweg-de Vries waves on time intervals of order log(1/h), resolving the cited open question; the proof combines the FPUT conservation law, h-uniform L2 local well-posedness, persistence of Sobolev regularity and a frequency-localized auxiliary equation. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30668v1. Further checking: Determine whether consolidating the author-proved estimates into Lemma 3.5 was a retained mathematical contribution or editorial synthesis; have an FPUT/KdV specialist check the long-time approximation, all uniform estimates and the claimed open-question resolution; compare v1 and v2 statement scope; establish novelty and priority; and independently reproduce any computation only in a controlled review. Keep provisional=1, coding confidence low, reviewStatus unreviewed and no Superhuman override.

Added flagged-provisional ID 3554 for Quadratic bounds for uncompletable words and matrix mortality. The source reports: The paper reports that every finite nonempty incomplete uniquely decipherable code with maximum word length k has an uncompletable word of length at most 4k^2-3k, with a polynomial-time construction and completeness decision; under the stated strongly-connected-component cycle-hitting hypothesis it derives a zero product of length at most 4n^2-3n for mortal families of nonnegative integer n-by-n matrices with joint spectral radius at most one, and gives a binary partial deterministic family establishing optimal quadratic order. The bounds and explicit-code algorithm are reported as proved in Lean. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30817v1. Further checking: Have formal-language/coding and matrix-semigroup specialists verify the code hypotheses, 4k^2-3k and 4n^2-3n arguments, the cycle-hitting condition, lower-bound construction and polynomial-work claim; independently replay the version-pinned Lean development; establish novelty and priority; and map Codex's contribution between proof discovery, formalization and exposition. Keep provisional=1, coding confidence low, reviewStatus unreviewed and no Superhuman override.

Added flagged-provisional ID 3555 for Riesz kernels of hyperbolic polynomials: positivity, admissible exponents and Jordan rigidity. The source reports: The v1 paper reports that every homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial p in n at least 2 variables that is positive on its hyperbolicity cone has p^(-alpha) completely monotone for every alpha at least 4096 n^2, independently of degree and coefficients; it also reports strict log-concavity and an explicit Gaussian comparison bound for the Riesz kernel under pointed-closure hypotheses, and that positive admissible exponents can accumulate at zero only for products of real linear forms. The retitled v2 materially expands the package; this proposed anchor is deliberately limited to the v1-supported core. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31592v1. Further checking: Have specialists in hyperbolic polynomials, complete monotonicity and Riesz kernels verify the saddle-point proof, alpha bounds, log-concavity, gap and linear-factor conclusions and their exact hypotheses; establish novelty and priority against Scott-Sokal and the cited positivity conjectures; compare and separately adjudicate the materially expanded v2 Jordan-rigidity/duality claims; independently reproduce the exact-arithmetic checks without executing the downloaded scripts; and reconstruct the retained author/model allocation claim by claim. Keep provisional=1, coding confidence low, reviewStatus unreviewed and no Superhuman override.

Added flagged-provisional ID 3556 for Semi-stable models, local heights and quadratic Chabauty for $X_0(N)^*$. The source reports: The official v1 abstract reports an explicit semi-stable minimal regular model for $X_0(N)^*$ at bad primes, existence for every squarefree $N>714$ of a global p-adic height whose bad-reduction contributions vanish, and new rational-point determinations for several $X_0(N)^*$ curves. Further checking: Further checking required: identify the exact auxiliary results and LLM drafts used in the 2026 phase; compare them with the author-checked final proofs; determine whether they materially enabled removal of the coprime-to-6 assumption; and independently check the semi-stable-model, p-adic-height, and rational-point claims. Added flagged-provisional ID 3557 for Distance-Shell Tomography: Geometric Certificates for Fault-Tolerant Sensing, Moment Compression, and Hypercube Equalization. The source reports: The paper reports a 14-statement package: exact four-corner interval-cut recovery on square grids after one erased report for populations of mass at most two; equivalent distance-sum compression; the exact corner-constrained grid optimum ceil(3(n+1)/2) for n>=3; hypercube equalizer bounds within one plus an infinite counterexample to a sourced exponential formula; the long-rectangle optimum; even bishop-board 2-domination; two exact Petersen values; and a connected real fractional-face counterexample. Primary source: https://data.palomar-registry.org/entries/PALOMAR-2026-10-04-000001-v1.json. Further checking: Further checking: Independently review all 14 selected statements, novelty and priority for each result group, exact-search and certificate claims, theorem/manuscript correspondence, and claim-level human/Codex/Claude allocation.

Added flagged-provisional ID 3558 for Gallai's conjecture with two exceptional even vertices. The source reports: The paper reports that a connected finite simple graph admits an edge partition into at most ceil(n/2) paths when its induced even-degree subgraph has at most two vertices of degree greater than three; it additionally exposes one designated positive even vertex twice at the ceiling budget, and treats two designated vertices within floor(n/2)+1 paths, with simultaneous ceiling only for odd order. Primary source: https://data.palomar-registry.org/entries/PALOMAR-2026-10-04-000006-v1.json. Further checking: Further checking: Obtain independent combinatorics review; check every hypothesis and path budget, manuscript/Lean correspondence, novelty against cited Fan/Botler results, inherited infrastructure, and exact human/Codex/Claude allocation.
